newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea asked parliament to secure its support for the government's tough reforms, including large budget cuts, reductions in subsidies, faster privatisation and liberalisation of markets.
Ciorbea presented the state of reforms so far, in line with the government's plans to prepare Romania in view of its joining the European Union and NATO.

* The pace of privatisation was swift this year when Romania put 800 companies into private hands, Ciorbea told parliament. By year 2000 some 70 percent of the gross domestic product will come from private companies, he said.
* The reform programme requires the efforts of all Romanian political parties and not just those of the ruling coalition, Ciorbea told the parliament.
* The opposition tabled a no-confidence motion on Tuesday saying the government had failed failed to fulfil its short-term programmes and to honour its own electoral promises.

Some 140 MPs from the opposition Party of Social Democracy, National Unity Party and the Greater Romania Party signed the motion, the first since the centrists took power. Parliament will debate the motion on Friday.
* The text of the motion attacks the government over its alleged lack of interest in the country's farming sector and the development of local capital markets.
The motion also says the government lacks a coherent strategy to restructure Romania's industry and that it turns a blind eye to the painful social costs of reforms.
* The motion concludes that the government is unable to rule and therefore has to be changed.

* For the first time in its history, Romania is no longer threatened by anyone, President Emil Constantinescu said during a visit to the Black Sea port of Mangalia, after the signing on Monday of a friendship treaty with Ukraine.
* Constantinescu said some one trillion lei had been recouped to the state budget following the anti-corruption campaign.
* The big BNS trade unions' confederation plans protests on June 11 against what it called the government's lack of transparency and coherence in adopting restructuring measures.
